::: {#sol-difference-regroup}

A counterexample (@def-counterexample) is one choice of $A$, $B$ and $C$ for which the two sides differ.
Let $A = B = C = \set{1}$.
Then

$$
\ba
\setdiff{A}{\paren{\setdiff{B}{C}}}
&= \setdiff{\set{1}}{\paren{\setdiff{\set{1}}{\set{1}}}}
\\&= \setdiff{\set{1}}{\emptyset}
\\&= \set{1},
\ea
$$

while

$$
\ba
\setdiff{\paren{\setdiff{A}{B}}}{C}
&= \setdiff{\paren{\setdiff{\set{1}}{\set{1}}}}{\set{1}}
\\&= \setdiff{\emptyset}{\set{1}}
\\&= \emptyset.
\ea
$$

The two sides differ, so the claim is false.

:::
